title: Two-stage Miller OTA
description: The classic two-stage Miller operational transconductance amplifier: a differential input stage (input pair + current-mirror load) driving a common-source second stage, with a compensation capacitor $C_c$ bridging the second stage (Miller pole-splitting). $C_c$ is the compensation knob: it sets the dominant pole and hence the unity-gain bandwidth GBW = $g_{m1}/(2*\pi*C_c)$. The feedforward path through $C_c$ creates a right-half-plane zero $z = g_{m2}/C_c$ that erodes phase; the $R_z = 1/g_{m2}$ nulling resistor removes it. The phase-margin and second-pole rows are ESTIMATE-grade small-signal approximations for sizing intuition — the simulator owns stability sign-off. Children evaluate in dependency order: the stage-1 mirror load first (its diode drop sets the stage-1 output DC), then the input device, then the stage-2 device and its load. On the demo NMOS table every device sizes against the same data, so the polarity-inverted loads keep their sign params at +1.

params.name: PM_target
params.note: phase-margin target; the PM row is estimate-grade

params.name: C1_est
params.note: stage-1 output node cap (stage-2 gate + drain parasitics + wiring); refine from the stage-2 device cgg plus extraction

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: nominal input common-mode at which the input device operating point is evaluated

params.name: Cc
params.note: Miller compensation cap: sets the dominant pole and GBW = gm1/(2*pi*Cc)

params.name: V1
params.note: stage-1 output DC level; sits about one mirror diode drop below VDD (retune with the stage-1-bias-consistent guardrail)

params.name: V_out2
params.note: stage-2 output DC level; sets both stage-2 devices' vds

params.name: vgs_est_in
params.note: estimate of the input-pair vgs used to place its drain; retune until input-bias-consistent is green

params.name: ld_sign
params.note: vds sign of the load tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: out_sign
params.note: vds sign of the stage-2 device table (PMOS common source): +1 for the N-style demo axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: Stage-1 mirror-load device
doc.description: One side of the stage-1 current-mirror load at half the tail current. Its diode drop sets the stage-1 output DC; its output conductance loads the first-stage gain.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current. Its drain sits at the stage-1 output DC (one mirror diode drop below VDD); its source sits one vgs below the input common mode.

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device carrying the full stage-2 current at the output DC level. Its gm sets the RHP zero, the second pole, and the nulling resistor; its gate capacitance dominates the stage-1 output node cap.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-2 current-source load
doc.description: The second-stage current-source load carrying the stage-2 current at the output DC level; its output conductance loads the second-stage gain.

rows.name: gm2
rows.note: stage-2 transconductance: sets the RHP zero, the second pole, and the nulling resistor

rows.name: GBW
rows.note: Miller-compensated unity-gain bandwidth (input gm into the compensation cap)

rows.name: wc
rows.note: angular unity-gain crossover (2*pi*GBW), the frequency the phase-margin estimate is read at

rows.name: z_rhp
rows.note: right-half-plane zero from the feedforward path through Cc; erodes phase near crossover

rows.name: p2
rows.note: non-dominant (output) pole ESTIMATE; C1_est is the stage-1 output-node cap — refine it from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

rows.name: Rz
rows.note: nulling resistor: Rz = 1/gm2 moves the RHP zero to infinity, cancelling the feedforward path

rows.name: PM
rows.note: ESTIMATE: crossover phase lag from the second pole plus the RHP zero (the nulling resistor removes the zero term). Two-pole-plus-zero approximation — the simulator owns stability sign-off

rows.name: SR
rows.note: the smaller slew limit: stage-1 tail charging Cc, or stage-2 current charging CL

rows.name: Av1
rows.note: stage-1 gain into the input-device and mirror-load output conductances

rows.name: Av2
rows.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

rows.name: Av
rows.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

rows.name: cgg2
rows.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est; compare to refine the estimate

rules.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target
the worse of the two slew limits meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target
ESTIMATE-grade phase margin; the simulator owns the real stability sign-off
the RHP zero must sit above crossover (equivalently gm2 >= gm1) or it collapses phase margin; the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor removes it if this is tight
stage-2 device saturated at the output DC level
stage-2 load saturated at the output DC level
the stage-1 output DC should equal VDD minus the mirror-load diode drop; retune V1 if this trips
the input-device drain placement uses vgs_est_in; retune it to the reported in__vgs if this trips
